## 1. Platform Strategy

### Target Platforms (Prioritized)

| Platform | Priority | Audience | Content Type | Frequency |
|----------|----------|----------|-------------|-----------|
| **LinkedIn** | P1 | CTOs, PMs, Eng Leads | Thought leadership, case studies, product updates | 3×/week |
| **Twitter/X** | P1 | Developers, tech community | Tips, release notes, community engagement | 5×/week |
| **Dev.to** | P2 | Developers, open-source community | Technical articles, tutorials, deep dives | 1×/week |
| **GitHub Discussions** | P2 | Contributors, power users | Feature discussions, Q&A, roadmap input | As needed |
| **YouTube** | P3 (Sprint 2+) | All audiences | Demo videos, tutorials, architecture walkthroughs | 1×/2 weeks |

### Platform-Specific Guidelines

**LinkedIn:**
- Professional tone; outcome-focused
- Include 1-2 relevant hashtags (not more)
- Optimal post length: 150-300 words
- Use carousels for multi-step concepts (Phase 1→4 flow)
- Tag relevant communities: #SoftwareEngineering #DevOps #ProductManagement

**Twitter/X:**
- Concise, punchy, developer-friendly tone
- Thread format for complex topics (max 5 tweets)
- Include code snippets or terminal output screenshots
- Hashtags: #AgenticSDLC #MultiAgent #CI_CD #OpenSource

**Dev.to:**
- Tutorial-style, hands-on content
- Include code examples and configuration snippets
- SEO-optimized titles ("How to..." / "Building a..." pattern)
- Cross-post to Hashnode and Medium (canonical URL on Dev.to)

## 5. Written Launch Content

### LinkedIn Post — Launch Announcement (Week 1, Monday)

Most software projects fail not because of bad code — but because strategy, architecture, UX, and go-to-market never talk to each other.

We built Agentic SDLC to change that.

It orchestrates 30+ specialized agents across 4 disciplines into a single delivery process. Before writing a line of code, you get:

• A validated business model and competitive analysis
• An architecture blueprint with security and compliance baked in
• A UX strategy with WCAG AA accessibility from Day 1
• A go-to-market framework with messaging, content, and analytics

Then it executes: sprint planning, automated CI/CD, quality gates, and KPI tracking — all with full audit trails.

This isn’t an AI code generator. It’s structured delivery for complete software solutions.

#AgenticSDLC #SoftwareEngineering #MultiAgent

### Twitter/X Thread — Launch (Week 1, Monday)

1/ We built a platform that orchestrates 30+ AI agents to create complete software solutions. Here’s how it works 🧵

2/ Phase 1: Business Analysis — 5 agents analyze your business model, market, financials, and competitive positioning. Output: validated requirements + risk matrix.

3/ Phase 2: Architecture — 6 agents design your system: cloud infra, security, data, DevOps, legal compliance. Output: architecture blueprint + dependency map.

4/ Phase 3: UX Design — 6 agents handle research, UI, accessibility, content strategy, and i18n. Output: component library + design system + a11y baseline.

5/ Phase 4: Marketing — 3 agents create brand identity, GTM strategy, and conversion framework. Then sprints ship production code with 80% test coverage gates.

The entire process is documented, traceable, and auditable. Check it out: github.com/RobertAgterhuis/myAgentic-IT-Project-team-V2

---

### LinkedIn Post — Risk Matrix (Week 1, Wednesday)

"We’ll figure out the risks later" is the most expensive sentence in software.

Before our first sprint started, Agentic SDLC had already identified 27 risks across 6 categories:

• Security: secret exposure, access control, dependency vulnerabilities
• Performance: scalability bottlenecks, response time thresholds
• Compliance: GDPR data flows, license compatibility, accessibility gaps
• Architecture: single points of failure, coupling, migration paths
• Business: market timing, resource constraints, scope creep
• Operations: monitoring, incident response, deployment rollbacks

Each risk has an owner, SLA, and escalation path — built into the sprint gate.

Risk management shouldn’t be a retrospective exercise. It should gate your sprint.

#RiskManagement #SoftwareEngineering #AgenticSDLC

## 6. Written Week 2 Content

### LinkedIn Post — Multi-Discipline Analysis (Week 2, Monday)

The most common startup failure mode isn't bad code. It's building the wrong thing — beautifully.

When engineering, product, UX, and marketing work in silos, each team optimizes for their own slice. The result? Architecture that doesn't support the business model. A marketing site that promises features the UX can't deliver. A compliance gap nobody noticed until launch week.

Agentic SDLC runs 30+ agents across 4 disciplines before writing a line of code:

Phase 1: Business analysts, domain experts, and financial modelers validate the opportunity.
Phase 2: Software architects, security architects, and DevOps engineers design the system.
Phase 3: UX researchers, designers, and accessibility specialists create the experience.
Phase 4: Brand strategists and growth marketers prepare the go-to-market.

Every phase is validated by Critic and Risk agents. Cross-team dependencies are mapped in a blocker matrix.

The result isn't just code — it's a complete solution where every decision traces back to a validated requirement.

#AgenticSDLC #ProductManagement #SoftwareArchitecture

---

### Twitter/X Thread — Critic + Risk Agent (Week 2, Tuesday)

1/ Your code review catches bugs. But who catches the strategic mistakes? Our Critic + Risk agent catches 5 categories of issues before they become sprint blockers 🔍

2/ 🔴 SECURITY: Secret exposure, access control gaps, dependency vulnerabilities. Every PR gets Gitleaks + Trivy scans automatically. Not as a suggestion — as a gate.

3/ 🟡 ARCHITECTURE: Over-coupling, missing fallbacks, scaling bottlenecks. The agent cross-references Phase 2 architecture decisions against actual implementation patterns.

4/ 🟠 COMPLIANCE: GDPR flows, license compatibility, WCAG violations. We found 3 accessibility gaps in our own token system and fixed them before Sprint 1.

5/ 🔵 BUSINESS: Scope drift, requirement gaps, misaligned priorities. Every sprint item traces back to validated Phase 1-4 decisions. Traceability isn't optional.

What does your risk process catch? 

#AgenticSDLC #RiskManagement #QualityEngineering

## 7. Dev.to Article — Privacy-First Analytics (Week 2, Wednesday)

**Title:** Privacy-First Analytics: How We Evaluate Matomo, Plausible, and Fathom

**Tags:** analytics, privacy, webdev, startup

**Cover image description:** Clean dashboard mockup with a shield icon — branded with Agentic SDLC color palette.

---

When we set out to add analytics to Agentic SDLC, we had one non-negotiable: no Google Analytics.

Not because GA is bad at what it does — it's excellent. But our platform handles sensitive project data (business models, architecture decisions, financial projections) and our users expect data residency they can verify. We needed analytics that align with the same privacy-first principles we build into the platform itself.

Here's how we evaluated three privacy-focused analytics tools and what we learned.

### The Evaluation Framework

We scored each tool across 8 dimensions on a 0-10 scale:

| Criteria | Weight | Matomo | Plausible | Fathom |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|--------|
| Data residency control | 15% | 10 | 7 | 6 |
| Feature completeness | 15% | 9 | 7 | 6 |
| GDPR compliance | 15% | 9 | 9 | 9 |
| Self-hosting capability | 10% | 10 | 8 | 5 |
| Setup complexity | 10% | 6 | 9 | 9 |
| Cost at scale | 10% | 9 | 7 | 6 |
| API/integration depth | 10% | 8 | 7 | 6 |
| Community & support | 15% | 8 | 8 | 7 |
| **Weighted Score** | | **8.6** | **8.3** | **7.0** |

### Why Matomo Won

**Data residency** was the deciding factor. Matomo self-hosted means our analytics data lives in the same infrastructure we control. No third-party processing, no data leaving our environment, no privacy policy gymnastics.

Key advantages:
- Full event tracking with custom dimensions
- Conversion funnels and A/B test integration
- Tag manager included (no Google Tag Manager dependency)
- Docker deployment aligns with our existing infrastructure
- Free for self-hosted; scales linearly with our own compute

### Where Plausible Shines

We're keeping Plausible as a lightweight secondary tool for our landing page. Its value proposition: under 1KB script, no cookies, instant setup. For a marketing landing page where we need basic traffic metrics without consent banners, it's the best option.

The decision matrix:
- **Webapp dashboard** → Matomo (full-featured, self-hosted)
- **Marketing landing page** → Plausible (lightweight, cookie-free)

### Implementation Approach

Our analytics baseline (SP-12-705) defines 5 primary KPI goals:

1. Health endpoint uptime (target: 99.5%)
2. Dashboard session duration (target: >2 min average)
3. Questionnaire completion rate (target: >60%)
4. API error rate (target: <1%)
5. Feature adoption rate (target: 3+ features per session)

Each goal maps to a Matomo goal configuration with custom event tracking.

### What We'd Recommend

If you're building a privacy-sensitive application:

1. **Start with your data residency requirements.** If you need full control, self-hosted Matomo is the only option that doesn't compromise.
2. **Don't over-engineer Day 1.** Start with 5 core KPIs, not 50. You can always add custom dimensions later.
3. **Use lightweight analytics for marketing pages.** Plausible or Fathom for landing pages; Matomo for the app.
4. **Document your analytics architecture decision.** We logged ours in `sp-12-705-analytics-baseline.md` with full scoring rationale.

Privacy-first doesn't mean feature-poor. It means intentional.

## 8. UTM Parameter Scheme

### Standard UTM Convention

All social links use this pattern:

```
https://[domain]/?utm_source=[platform]&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=[campaign]&utm_content=[content-id]
```

| Parameter | Convention | Examples |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| `utm_source` | Platform name (lowercase) | `linkedin`, `twitter`, `devto`, `github` |
| `utm_medium` | Always `social` for organic posts | `social` |
| `utm_campaign` | Sprint or launch identifier | `sprint-1-launch`, `week-2-content` |
| `utm_content` | Post identifier | `intro-elevator-pitch`, `critic-risk-thread`, `analytics-article` |

### Example Links

- LinkedIn intro post: `?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=sprint-1-launch&utm_content=intro-elevator-pitch`
- Twitter CI/CD thread: `?utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=sprint-1-launch&utm_content=cicd-showcase`
- Dev.to analytics article: `?utm_source=devto&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=week-2-content&utm_content=analytics-article`

## 9. Written Week 2 Content (Day 7 Additions)

### LinkedIn Post — Real Sprint Case Study (Week 2, Thursday)

From requirements to running code: a real sprint in our system.

Sprint 1 of Agentic SDLC started on March 10 with 15 backlog items across 4 tracks: business governance, technical infrastructure, UX/accessibility, and marketing launch.

Here's what happened in 7 working days:

🔧 **Tech track:** 99 automated tests across 5 suites. 80% coverage gate enforced in CI. 8-job pipeline including lint, security scanning (Gitleaks + Trivy), Docker build, staging deployment, integration tests, and smoke tests. Zero secrets in code — verified on every push.

📋 **Business track:** 4 governance documents signed (privacy policy, cookie policy, terms of service, acceptable use policy). Legal compliance baseline established before any user-facing feature shipped.

🎨 **UX track:** WCAG AA audit baseline at 91%. Design tokens locked (v2.0.0) with versioned color, typography, and spacing scales. Component inventory mapped to accessibility requirements.

📣 **Marketing track:** Complete GTM messaging framework. 5-email welcome sequence written. Content calendar across LinkedIn, Twitter/X, and Dev.to. Privacy-first analytics (Matomo + Plausible) evaluated and selected.

Every item traces back to a validated requirement from Phase 1-4 analysis. Every risk has an owner and an SLA.

This is what "sprint-ready output" means — not just a JIRA backlog, but a cross-team execution framework.

Next week: Sprint 1 closes. All 15 items target 100%.

#AgenticSDLC #SprintPlanning #SoftwareEngineering #ProductManagement

## 10. Written Week 2 Content — Day 8 Additions

### Twitter/X Post — Testing Showcase (Week 2, Friday)

99 tests. 5 suites. 0.5 seconds. Every push.

Here's our Sprint 1 testing stack for @AgenticSDLC:

🧪 Unit: 27 middleware tests
🔗 Integration: 31 server + health endpoint tests
💨 Smoke: 23 critical journey tests (7 groups)
📊 Coverage gate: 80% minimum, enforced in CI
🔒 Security: Gitleaks + Trivy on every push

The smoke suite covers:
→ Landing page loads
→ Health endpoints respond
→ API routes return valid JSON
→ Session management works
→ Security headers present
→ Decisions API accessible

Total test time: <1 second. No Playwright. No browser. Pure HTTP-level testing.

CI pipeline: 8 jobs, 7 active. Build → Lint → Security → Test → Integration → Smoke → Deploy.

Privacy-first. Open-source. Multi-agent.
